title: NIS2: does it apply to my business?
notes: Format "Was tust du?" (Format-Bibel 1.0), Reihe "Gilt das für uns?". F1 EN (localised from the DE spec), series Does this apply to us? Example case staged: firm, customer, email and time are invented. Rules from S1 to S3, re-read 02.11.2026; German specifics (BSI scope check, BSIG supply-chain rules) are labelled as German. No legal verdict, no legal advice: the answer ends with a check, interpretation and a pointer to legal advice. The old plan ai_security-20261114-2-en.json stays unchanged.

unverified: Exact thresholds (staff, turnover): not named; checked via a scope check.
National laws outside Germany: not covered in detail; only the fact that member states had to transpose NIS2 into national law (S1).
No legal advice; whether the example firm is covered is deliberately not answered.
Example case (electrical contractor, Example Energy, the confirmation request) is invented and marked as an example.

Newly checked 02.11.2026 (S3): under Germany's BSIG, not every supplier is indirectly obliged; covered entities must hold their suppliers to matching security requirements. Applying this to the example firm is interpretation.
European Commission proposal of 20.01.2026 for targeted NIS2 amendments (S1): not used.

hook_candidates.spoken: NIS2 is only for big companies? Then why is your customer asking you about it?
hook_candidates.on_screen: Only big firms? Then why ask you?

hook_candidates.spoken: NIS2 applies to every business? As a rule, it doesn't.
NIS2 covers eighteen critical sectors across the EU.
One compromised supplier can bring down IT systems, says Germany's BSI.

beats.spoken: Thursday, 11:20 a.m. An email from the energy company, your biggest customer: We're implementing NIS2. Please confirm our rules for service providers. Does that apply to you now?

You're a small business. Your trade: electrical work. Your customer: an energy company. Sounds like: this doesn't affect us. According to the European Commission, NIS2 applies as a rule to medium-sized and large entities in eighteen critical sectors.

fact.text: NIS2: mostly medium and large entities, 18 sectors.

beats.spoken: What do you reply? A: We're too small, this doesn't affect us. B: So now we're covered by NIS2 too. C: Check first, then clarify with the customer. Remember your choice.

options.text: Now we're covered by NIS2 too
Check first, then ask the customer

beats.spoken: C is the safe route. In Germany, the BSI offers a scope check with a questionnaire, as a first assessment that isn't legally binding. On A: covered customers must hold their suppliers to security requirements. On B: the law doesn't automatically oblige every supplier.

card.title: Check first, then answer
card.sub: use a scope check, e.g. the BSI's

beats.spoken: And if the result stays unclear? NIS2 is national law in each EU country, and a scope check is no binding answer. For your specific case, you need legal advice. This video isn't legal advice.

card.title: Ask, don't guess
card.sub: a scope check isn't a binding answer

beats.spoken: Many aren't covered directly, but feel it through customers. Check first, then answer. What would you have picked? Tell me in the comments.
